editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, and it keeps its meaning throughout, e.g. "mas mahigpit na matantya ang hangganan ng sensitivity sa mga error" for "more tightly bound the sensitivity to errors" in the SLC entry, and "pag-absorb ng mga inverse ng mga natutunang noise channel sa mga observable" for PNA.

The meaning holds throughout and I found nothing that would mislead a learner. The three pre-flight checks, the TEM-vs-PEC comparison with fewer shots, and the explanation of circuit functions versus application functions all match the English. A native editor would still fix a few spots. In [7], "ngayon ay i-validate ng run()" uses the infinitive/imperative verb form where the ongoing form "vina-validate" is needed. In [49], "matapos matapos" is a clumsy doubled word. In [64], "idulot" means "cause" or "bring about", but the English "bring" here means to bring in or apply knowledge. In [63], "out of the box" becomes the stiff "nang wala nang karagdagang gawin".

examples.source: and `run()` now validates both before it submits a job.
examples.translation: at ngayon ay i-validate ng `run()` ang pareho bago mag-submit ng job.
examples.suggested: at vina-validate na ngayon ng `run()` ang dalawang ito bago mag-submit ng job.
examples.why: The infinitive/imperative form 'i-validate' is ungrammatical for a statement of fact; the ongoing form is needed.

examples.source: Finally, after a Qiskit Function is complete, you can inspect how much time is spent
examples.translation: Sa huli, matapos matapos ang isang Qiskit Function, maaari mong siyasatin
examples.suggested: Sa huli, kapag tapos na ang isang Qiskit Function, maaari mong suriin
examples.why: 'matapos matapos' is an awkward doubled word that makes the reader stumble.

examples.source: and instead hope to bring their domain knowledge to advance quantum computing algorithms
examples.translation: at sa halip ay inaasahan nilang idulot ang kanilang domain knowledge
examples.suggested: at sa halip ay nais nilang gamitin ang kanilang domain knowledge
examples.why: 'idulot' means cause or bring about, which is the wrong sense of 'bring' here; the sentence reads oddly.

examples.source: to make utility-grade performance accessible out of the box
examples.translation: upang gawing accessible ang utility-grade performance nang wala nang karagdagang gawin
examples.suggested: upang agad na magamit ang utility-grade performance nang walang dagdag na setup
examples.why: The rendering of 'out of the box' is stiff and grammatically clunky.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful across all five short entries, and the Taglish reads naturally, e.g. "Na-release ang skill na `migrate-qiskit-ibm-runtime`, para sa pag-migrate ng code na `qiskit-ibm-runtime`"; "Setyembre 2026" and "Changelog ng Qiskit skills" are correct.

The translation is faithful and reads naturally in casual register. In [9] the hedge is kept: "maaaring mas mabilis at makapagbigay ng mas magandang resulta" preserves "might be faster", and "transpiler pass" and "transpilation" are used consistently.

Nothing in the translation would mislead a learner. Every feature claim matches the English, including "nang hindi kailangang muling buuin ang buong compiler pipeline" and "lalo na ang mga Clifford+T target". Entries [9] and [11] each open an ay-inversion with a bare "Mga ..." subject and no "Ang", which reads as calqued English. Entry [9] also stacks "pagpapahusay / nagpapahusay / pinapahusay" in one sentence, and a native editor would smooth that out.

examples.source: Upgrades and Rust-driven performance enhancements to `VF2Layout` and `VF2PostLayout` improve the speed and scalability ... reducing compilation overhead and improving fidelity
examples.translation: Mga upgrade at Rust-driven na pagpapahusay sa performance sa `VF2Layout` at `VF2PostLayout` ay nagpapahusay sa bilis at scalability ... binabawasan ang compilation overhead at pinapahusay ang fidelity
examples.suggested: Ang mga upgrade at Rust-driven na pagpapabilis sa `VF2Layout` at `VF2PostLayout` ay nagpapabuti sa bilis at scalability ..., kaya nababawasan ang compilation overhead at tumataas ang fidelity
examples.why: The subject has no 'Ang' before 'Mga', and three forms of 'pahusay' in one sentence make it read stiff and machine-like.

examples.source: Performance and feature enhancements for transpilation to early fault-tolerant targets ... help users
examples.translation: Mga pagpapahusay sa performance at feature para sa transpilation ... ay tumutulong sa mga user
examples.suggested: Ang mga pagpapahusay sa performance at feature para sa transpilation ... ay tumutulong sa mga user
examples.why: An ay-inversion subject needs 'Ang mga'. Starting with a bare 'Mga ...' is a calque of the English sentence order.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful across the file. The QPU retirement dates, the rep_delay ranges, the "no sooner than" deprecation in [287] and the Qiskit Runtime rename architecture in [42]-[51] all match the English. One small date slip needs fixing: in [267], "on or around 2 June 2025" became "sa o pagkatapos ng" ("on or after"). The rest is polish. Month names are inconsistent: "Setyembre/Agosto/Oktubre" appear next to untranslated "July/April/March/February/January 2026". Some headings were left in English ("Upcoming retirements", "`ibm_torino` is now retired"), and the Accordion titles are mixed ("Third Quarter" in one place, "Ikatlong quarter" in another). There are also a few calques ("mas accessible na kailanman", "iyo lamang na mga workload", "pinaka-mataas ang performance na mga").

examples.source: will be no longer supported on or around 2 June 2025
examples.translation: hindi na masusuportahan sa o pagkatapos ng 2 Hunyo 2025
examples.suggested: hindi na masusuportahan sa o malapit sa 2 Hunyo 2025
examples.why: 'On or around' became 'on or after', which changes the timing of the cutoff. Elsewhere the file correctly uses 'sa o malapit sa'.
Month names are inconsistent: some are localized (Setyembre, Agosto, Oktubre, Hunyo) and others are left in English (July, April, March, February, January).
'Mas ... na kailanman' is a word-for-word calque of 'than ever'. 'Higit kailanman' is the natural Tagalog idiom.

examples.source: The platform now displays only your workloads by default.
examples.translation: Ipinapakita na ngayon ng platform ang iyo lamang na mga workload bilang default.
examples.suggested: Ang sarili mo lamang na mga workload ang ipinapakita na ngayon ng platform bilang default.
examples.why: 'Ang iyo lamang na mga workload' is stiff word order that a native technical writer would not use.
This heading was left in English (as was the one in [94]), while the nearby headings such as [80] and [85] are translated.
